content.value_statement: Frontend reviews often miss accessibility, data boundary, and component ownership issues. This skill gives Claude and Codex a focused checklist for Dify React and Next.js code reviews.
actual_capabilities: Reviews pending frontend changes, named files, or pasted diffs under Dify web paths.
Checks accessibility issues such as labels, focus handling, keyboard access, and popup reachability.
Applies Dify UI and Base UI rules for primitives, overlays, forms, tokens, and component boundaries.
Reviews React component ownership, state modeling, effects, props, and feature organization.
Checks data query contracts, mutations, SSR boundaries, URL state, and local storage usage.
Reports findings with severity, file location, reasoning, and concrete fix direction.
limitations: It is tailored to Dify frontend conventions and may not fit unrelated React projects.
It relies on readable local files or provided diffs for accurate line-level findings.
It does not implement fixes unless the user asks for review plus changes.
Current external guidance may require a permitted network fetch before final accessibility findings.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request before merge
use_cases.description: Check changed React and Next.js files for user-visible regressions, accessibility problems, and test gaps.

use_cases.title: Audit a Dify UI component refactor
use_cases.description: Verify that component ownership, primitive usage, focus behavior, and interaction contracts remain correct.

use_cases.title: Validate risky frontend data flows
use_cases.description: Review query keys, mutations, SSR boundaries, URL state, and workspace or auth assumptions before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review my pending frontend changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of current working tree changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-code-review skill to review my pending Dify frontend changes. Focus on correctness, accessibility, and clear fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a specific component file
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for one file or area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-code-review skill to review web/path/to/component.tsx. Check component ownership, Dify UI usage, accessibility, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an overlay or form flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-code-review skill to audit this dialog or form flow. Verify labels, focus behavior, keyboard access, disabled states, and popup reachability.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a release-blocking frontend review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-code-review skill for a thorough release-blocking review. Prioritize P0 and P1 issues in data contracts, SSR behavior, accessibility, performance, and tests.

output_examples.input: Review the pending changes to a settings dialog.
output: Each finding includes a file and line when available.
The response explains why the issue matters and gives a concrete fix direction.

output_examples.input: Review a component refactor with no issues found.
output_examples.output: No issues found. The response also notes which tests were not run and any residual review limits.

output_examples.input: Audit a form that uses custom controls.
output: The review checks accessible names, field labels, keyboard behavior, disabled states, and error recovery.
It avoids style-only feedback unless it causes a user-visible issue.

best_practices: Provide the exact files, diff, or pull request scope you want reviewed.
Mention whether the review should be quick, thorough, or release-blocking.
Run relevant tests or share test constraints so the review can include residual risk.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for backend-only code under api paths.
Do not ask for broad style preferences without a concrete frontend risk.
Do not treat pasted snippets as complete when surrounding ownership or accessibility context matters.

faq.question: What projects is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for Dify frontend code, especially web, packages/dify-ui, React, Next.js, and TypeScript changes.

faq.question: Can it review accessibility issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It treats keyboard access, focus behavior, labels, disabled states, and popup reachability as correctness concerns.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides review and may recommend tests, but test execution depends on the user request and available project setup.

faq.question: Will it fix the findings?
faq.answer: Not by default. The skill asks the assistant to report findings unless the user explicitly requests implementation.

faq.question: Why does it reference external guidelines?
faq.answer: It asks reviewers to fetch current Web Interface Guidelines when UI or accessibility findings need the latest baseline.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
